display.title: Episode 41: The Return of Little Tzip Tzip
display.summary_short: A little bird finds a bad smell in every direction until her mother wipes her nose: a gentle story about looking at others with a good eye and fixing our own faults first.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi opens by marveling at the mail pouring in and explains that it is a mitzvah to be happy, as Dovid HaMelech says, 'Serve Hashem with joy', before a happy march. Two young Tzivos Hashem members in the studio say they love the stories, especially the mysteries, and everyone says the Shema together. Story time: Tzip Tzip, a very little bird, learns to fly, and her mother sends her out to discover a world full of good things. But in the east, the west, the north and the south, everything smells bad, and she keeps flying home, until her mother finds a speck of dirt on the tip of her nose and wipes it clean. Uncle Yossi explains the lesson: to love a fellow Jew we must look at him with an ayin tovah, a good eye; the Baal Shem Tov taught that a fault we see in others is like a mirror of our own, and the Sages say to correct ourselves first. After a sponsor message, he speaks about Jewish unity through Torah and invites every child to get a letter in the new children's Sefer Torah and to share the mitzvah with family and friends.
display.lesson: Look at others with a good eye; the faults we notice in others are often our own, so correct yourself first.

date.note: Weekly estimate is 14 Sept 1982 (26 Elul 5742), but the show never mentions Rosh Hashanah and says 'it's only a few weeks that we're on the air'; possibly an early show re-aired or misnumbered.
